name: aomega-m3-wronskian-casoratian-gauge
description: The Casoratian identity applied to the descendant operators of 4_1, 5_2 and the (-2,3,7) pretzel: the Wronskian determinant ratio from the end coefficients, the palindrome gauge that trivialises it, and GGM (276) recovered exactly for 5_2.

parameters.casoratian_rule: det W_{m+1}/det W_m = (-1)^r a_0/a_r  [GGM Thm 16(c), GK13 Lem 4.7]

pretzel.why_not_palindromic: END-pair roots exist but at least one INTERIOR pair fails at every one of them

data.pretzel_why_not_palindromic: END-pair roots exist but at least one INTERIOR pair fails at every one of them

verdict: DERIVED: the per-knot GL(r) normalisation is NOT a free choice — GGM's Theorem 16(c) names the mechanism, the Casoratian identity det W_{m+1}/det W_m = (-1)^r a_0/a_r, which depends on the operator's END coefficients alone. Calibrated on GGM's own printed 4_1 operator (135), the rule returns their printed (136) ratio x^3 (G1). Applied to the operators #7333 derived: 4_1 ratio Q**2/XR**2, 5_2 -Q**3, pretzel Q**8. Each operator has a distinguished PALINDROME gauge, the one making the ratio (-1)^r; for 5_2 it is lambda = Q, and in it our N(X) is GGM's printed (276) coefficients (1, s, s, 1) exactly (G2) — which is why their 5_2 Wronskian is m-independent. The pretzel's gauge is lambda = None, i.e. q^(None); whether that lies in the q^(1/2) ring the level-2 grading lives in: False (T1). When no gauge exists the reason is stated rather than left as a bare absence: END-pair roots exist but at least one INTERIOR pair fails at every one of them, failing index pairs [1, 2, 4, 5].

assertions.name: G1-the Casoratian rule (-1)^r a_0/a_r applied to GGM's OWN printed 4_1 operator (135) returns their printed Wronskian ratio x^3 of (136) — the rule is calibrated against a published answer before being applied to our operators
G2-our derived 5_2 N(X), in its palindrome gauge, is GGM's printed (276) coefficients (1, s, s, 1) EXACTLY — so the gauge is not a free knob, it is the one GGM already use
G3-5_2 admits a palindrome gauge at all, which is what makes GGM's Wronskian m-INDEPENDENT (their sec-015: det W_{m+1} = det W_m) — the ratio is (-1)^r there

G4-the positive-lambda restriction costs nothing at even rank: j and r-j share parity, so lambda^j and lambda^{r-j} have the same sign for EVERY real lambda and a negative gauge imposes the identical conditions — the T1 negative is not an artifact of the search range
T1-the pretzel's degree-6 N(X) admits a palindrome gauge lying in the q^{1/2} ring that the level-2 structure lives in (#7333: sigma is odd exactly when q is half-integral)
